source_basis: canonical verses 1–10 from Stotra Nidhi, linked in content/sources/d032/source-custody.json

matsya.form: Divine avatar as a fish, from a small luminous fish in stanza 2 to the immense oceanic fish of stanzas 6–10.
matsya.continuity: Deep indigo-blue upper scales, warm cream underside, calm clear fish eyes, exactly one prominent horn high on the forehead from the giant form onward; natural coherent fins, gills, tail, and single continuous fish body. Small form in stanza 2 is the same fish.
matsya.anatomy: Fish anatomy only. No humanoid torso, arms, hands, legs, crown, peacock feather, or copied Guruvayurappan humanoid identity. Single horn stays visible and is the boat-tether point in stanzas 7–8.
never: no extra horns or duplicated fins
no metallic shine, gloss, text, or photorealism

satyavrata.form: A dignified South Indian sage-king, shown as the same adult man in stanzas 2–9.
satyavrata.continuity: Warm medium-brown skin, dark hair gathered simply, neat moustache, cream dhoti with muted ochre/maroon edge, sacred thread; practical ascetic simplicity, no oversized crown.
satyavrata.anatomy: Natural adult proportions, exactly two attached arms and two legs; scene actions use clear connected hands.
never: no costume or facial redesign across scenes
no royal spectacle or modern items

hayagriva.form: The asura Hayagriva is a single horse-headed adult humanoid adversary, matching the source image as a subject cue.
hayagriva.continuity: One coherent equine head with natural muzzle and ears on a distinct humanlike torso, dark maroon/earth-ochre garments and restrained ornaments.
hayagriva.anatomy: Exactly two natural attached arms and two legs; no extra deity limbs. Keep all anatomy connected.
never: do not confuse the asura with a Matsya or Guruvayurappan form
no grotesque monster features or gore
no extra horse heads, limbs, or duplicated bodies

saptarishis.form: Seven distinct mature sages, together only in stanzas 5–8 and returned to their places in stanza 9.
saptarishis.continuity: Seven individually distinguishable older men in simple cream and ochre ascetic garments, varied natural hair/beard arrangements, prayer beads and staffs only where they fit hands.
saptarishis.anatomy: Every visible sage has one head, two arms, two hands, and two legs with natural proportions; no clones or merged bodies.
never: do not make the group ambiguous or duplicated

vasuki.form: The king of serpents is one living naga, used as the line securing the boat to Matsya’s horn in stanza 7 and remaining attached as they travel in stanza 8.
vasuki.continuity: One continuous deep green/earth-ochre serpent body, one recognizable hooded head, calm alert face, restrained painted markings.
vasuki.anatomy: The full body visibly connects boat and single fish horn; the curve is taut enough to read as a tether but not cutting into either.
never: no multiple detached heads or coils
do not borrow Adishesha’s multi-hood canopy
no attack posture, fangs, or human limbs

scene_contracts.brahma: Use existing approved art/bible/characters/brahma/character.json and its exact approved image only for identity/iconography when Brahma is in frame: four heads total, three faces visible frontally; exactly four distinct connected arms/hands.
scene_contracts.flood_boat: In stanzas 6–8 the boat signifies Earth as source imagery states. Keep it a single stable boat with all occupants seated/holding safely; do not make it a globe or split island unless the supplied scene photo clearly does so.
scene_contracts.s09_s10_violence: Depict the sourced defeat of Hayagriva with non-graphic restraint; no blood or exposed anatomy.
